body: I think this would be better suited under the `utf16` section, as that's the ordering generally used elsewhere.

Come to think of it, all the other static from-encoding functions could just be inlined in the header, couldn't they? I'm not saying that's necessarily in the scope of this PR, but something to consider for the future.
I agree, and I've been planning to do that. Small steps :)

Quick fix due to [build failing](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/actions/runs/12693042092/job/35379786940?pr=101352) because of erroneous cache restores.

I have [previously established](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100293#issuecomment-2556731863) that including a non-generated file explicitly solves such cache issues for good.
For consistency, the same changes can be done in `gdextension_string_new_with_wide_chars`, `gdextension_string_new_with_utf32_chars_and_len` and `gdextension_string_new_with_wide_chars_and_len`.

Is `_strlen_clipped()` correct here?

That will mean that it'll clip the ending to the first `0` it encounters. However, looking at `String::copy_from_unchecked()` it seems like it would just take the length, allowing `0` to exist in the string. So, adding `_strlen_clipped()` would change behavior here.

However, I don't know if the original behavior is what we want or not, or if people depend on being able to make `String`s with `0`s in them via this function.
`String::parse_latin1()` also seems like it will allow `0`s in the string, so this would be another behavior change.

> Is `_strlen_clipped()` correct here?

Unfortunately, yes! `String((const char32_t *)p_contents, p_char_count)` calls `parse_utf32(p_cstr, p_clip_to_len);` which in turn calls `parse_utf32(StrRange(p_cstr, p_cstr ? _strlen_clipped(p_cstr, p_clip_to) : 0));`. `copy_from_unchecked` is not involved.
The behavior should be the same as before. It remains questionable that this is how we _want_ it to behave, though.

I guess my change _does_ imply one change in that it doesn't check the incoming pointer for `null`. That should probably still be done (Edit: Done).
`_strlen_clipped` clips the string at the first 0, so it would prevent this from happening.

> which in turn calls `parse_utf32(StrRange(p_cstr, p_cstr ? _strlen_clipped(p_cstr, p_clip_to) : 0));`. `copy_from_unchecked` is not involved.

But doesn't `parse_utf32(const StrRange<char32_t> &p_cstr)` call to `copy_from_unchecked`?

> `_strlen_clipped` clips the string at the first 0, so it would prevent this from happening.

Right. I'm saying before this PR, looks like `0` would be allowed in the string, but that after this PR (because of the `_strlen_clipped()` call) it will no longer allow `0` in the string, because it would clip the length at the first `0`.
NUL should not exist in the Godot strings, `copy_from_unchecked` was checking for NUL it before #99816.
Ah, ok, so then it wouldn't be a behavior change. Thanks!
It we never should have been allowing `0` in Godot strings anyway (per @bruvzg above) then we can resolve this one too

Shouldn't it return a CharString (like the `latin1` above) ? Or maybe be called `parse_latin1` instead ?
Because that would mean that : 
```
String str("Hello");
CharString s1 = str.latin1();
String s2 = String::latin1("Hello"); // This seems like a shorthand for above, but it is not, one is CharString and the other is String
```

Wouldn't it make more sense to have it return a CharString, and maybe have a static parse_latin1 too ?
Well I see that utf8 has the same behaviour, so at least it is consistent.
I agree, the naming is unnecessarily confusing. I opted it to be consistent for now but agree renaming the bunch may be a good idea.
